title: SunCar Stock Faces Major Test After 26% Revenue Surge
detail:
SunCar Stock Faces Major Test After 26% Revenue Surge
Moz Farooque ACCA
Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:49 AM MST 2 min read

Trade SDA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

SunCar Technology Group (NASDAQ:SDA) expects revenue to surge 26% during the first nine months of 2026, while swinging from losses to profitability, signaling improving momentum in its Chinese automotive technology business. However, the company faces a demanding fourth-quarter sales target to meet its ambitious full-year outlook.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 1 Warning Sign with SDA.

Is SDA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

SDA GF Value chart

SunCar operates digital platforms connecting Chinese motorists with automotive insurance, maintenance and other vehicle-related services. It generates revenue through its Auto eInsurance, Auto Services and Technology Services divisions, working with automakers, insurers and enterprise partners.

In its November 6 announcement, SunCar projected preliminary, unaudited nine-month revenue of approximately $426.4 million, up 26% year over year.

Net income is expected to reach $5.8 million, reversing a $4.1 million loss during the comparable 2025 period.

The improvement marks five consecutive profitable quarters beginning in the third quarter of 2025.

Auto eInsurance led the expansion, with revenue climbing 32% to $197.4 million. Auto Services revenue increased 22% to $185.4 million, while Technology Services grew 19% to $43.6 million.

SunCar's growth follows expanding relationships within China's electric vehicle ecosystem, including Huawei-linked automotive brands.

Despite the encouraging results, management maintained its full-year revenue forecast of $600 million.

That leaves approximately $173.6 million in required fourth-quarter sales, compared with roughly $149.9 million generated in the third quarter, implying sequential growth of nearly 16%.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest near-term test is whether SunCar can deliver that fourth-quarter acceleration without sacrificing profitability.

Investors should closely monitor insurance renewal revenue, operating margins and cash generation as the business expands.

The company's first-half adjusted EBITDA reached $9.4 million, compared with $2.5 million a year earlier, underscoring improving operating efficiency.

Investors should also assess whether the preliminary nine-month figures hold up in finalized results.

Meeting the $600 million annual target while maintaining profitability would strengthen confidence in SunCar's business model. A fourth-quarter slowdown or weaker margins could challenge the turnaround narrative.

Tripadvisor downgraded by BofA as CEO and CFO exits add risk Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Tripadvisor Inc (NASDAQ:TRIP) earnings recovery could take longer than expected, Bank of America warned, downgrading the company to "underperform" from "buy" and cutting its target to $8 from $15.

The bank cited slowing growth and traffic disruption, with the CEO and CFO departing over the next few months during restructuring, adding execution risk.

Third-quarter revenue fell 11% against guidance for a 7% to 10% year-over-year decline, while revenue and EBITDA missed Wall Street expectations, according to BofA.

Tripadvisor's fourth-quarter outlook points to further weakness, with revenue guided down by a low-teens percentage versus Wall Street's expected 5% decline.

Bank of America consequently cut its fourth-quarter 2026 revenue estimate to $310 million from $332 million and EBITDA to $17 million from $40 million.

The reductions extend into its annual forecasts, with 2026 and 2027 revenue now expected to fall 9.6% and 5.0%, versus 7.5% and 1.1% previously.

BofA lowered corresponding EBITDA estimates to $180 million and $174 million from $221 million and $235 million, citing higher sales and marketing spending.

Those forecasts reflect Tripadvisor's search engine optimization and AI-driven traffic disruption, softer US-Europe demand, and increasing competition, according to Bank of America.

The bank expects search-related traffic losses through 2027, while management's growth-over-margin priority that year and greater reliance on paid marketing could delay earnings recovery.

BofA therefore remains uncertain about Viator's return to sustainable double-digit growth with improved marketing efficiency.

There are encouraging signs, however, as Bank of America said AI-referred Experiences traffic converts well despite small volumes, while management is directing product, engineering and analytics resources toward Viator.

Potential challenges to the bank's cautious view include a strategic-review outcome involving a sale or further portfolio actions.

Other upside risks include faster Experiences growth as macroeconomic and geopolitical pressures ease, AI and new paid channels scale, and restructuring and marketing efficiency support margin recovery.

BofA also cited approximately $685 million in net TheFork proceeds as providing flexibility to reduce debt and potentially resume capital returns.

title: Boot Barn has a plan to win holiday shoppers, and BofA likes it
detail:
Boot Barn has a plan to win holiday shoppers, and BofA likes it
Peace Longe, Celine Provini

BAC

Trading disclosure

The holiday season is coming, and Boot Barn (BOOT) is getting ready for the shopping that comes with it.

Boot Barn operates more than 580 stores across 49 U.S. states, selling cowboy boots, denim, work boots, and ranch apparel. Although the stock has had a tough 2026, Wall Street wants to see whether the company can pull off a strong holiday quarter. 

BOOT shares are down about 28% this year, but the stock has increased by roughly 20% over the past five trading days. That recent bounce followed the company's second-quarter results. Bank of America then added another round of support.

In early November, BofA analyst Chris Nardone, who covers softlines and consumer retail for the bank, met with Boot Barn's management and was impressed by their plans.

Because of that and the company's recent results, he kept his Buy rating and $166 price target on BOOT. That price target implies about a 24% increase from the stock's recent $133 share price.

A women's boot refresh aimed squarely at Black Friday

Boot Barn's leadership has been clear that their women's fashion boots are a weak spot for the company. However, CEO John Hazen told BofA that the company is moving fast to fix that.

Boot Barn is bringing in more color options and higher-priced fashion styles in time for Black Friday. The company has also featured the new boots in Boot Barn's holiday gift guide and national TV ads so they can bring more shoppers into stores.

Also read: Kroger cuts discounts, promises pricing changes

Men's boots are also showing a few signs of weakness. In Boot Barn's fiscal second quarter of 2027, sales of men's rubber-soled Western boots slowed. The company's management isn't sure yet whether the reason was the warm weather or customers being more careful with their spending because of the economic situation. 

Even so, the company's management remains hopeful about the holiday season. In the company's October earnings release filed with the SEC, Hazen said Boot Barn is "excited about the holiday season," pointing to refreshed products, improved stores, and a bigger national marketing push.

Boot Barn is leaning on a refreshed women's boot assortment and a national TV ad push to drive traffic into its stores this holiday season.Darya Komarova / Getty Images
Why BofA still sees Boot Barn stock as a bargain

BofA still sees BOOT as a bargain because of its valuation. Boot Barn trades at about 14 times its expected earnings over the next two years.

Nardone thinks that's low for Boot Barn, especially since he expects the company to grow its earnings by 15% next year, once tariff refunds are stripped out. In the BofA note shared with me, Nardone described the stock as "cheap relative to its growth profile."

Investing.com — With Citigroup (NYSE:C) expecting the Federal Reserve to hold off on rate cuts until June 2027, investors are sorting banks by who can keep earning while rates stay high. JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) is the usual answer, at nearly 14 times earnings, and Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) has barely moved in a year.

Investors have been willing to pay for safety, but it's Citigroup that gained 29.6% over that stretch and still trades at 11.4 times earnings.

That lower multiple shows lingering doubt about a bank still in the middle of a restructuring, and a monthly data-driven screen can test it against each new set of results. ProPicks AI, InvestingPro's AI-driven stock-picking service, added Citigroup to its Beat the S&P 500 strategy for November. The bank shares that line-up with an online travel booking leader, a high-margin commercial biopharma company and a commercial jet-turbine maker.

See the full list of AI-picked holdings: Explore the Beat the S&P 500 strategy on InvestingPro

Cutting Costs While the Services Franchise Grows

Citigroup's latest quarter backed the turnaround plan with results. Earnings per share of $2.85 beat estimates by 7.5%, revenue rose 8% in the strongest third quarter for revenue in a decade, and return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) reached 11.5%, up 180 basis points from a year earlier. Management lifted its full-year ROTCE target to above 11%.

Most of that growth came from the units Citi is betting on. Services revenue grew 15% with a 31.2% ROTCE, Wealth revenue also rose 15% on $38 billion of net new investment assets, and equity capital markets revenue jumped 77%, helped by leading six of the largest equity deals of the quarter. Meanwhile the efficiency ratio improved to 58.5% from 64.7%, with more than $1 billion of severance booked this year and stranded costs trimmed to about a $100 million quarterly run rate.

Consumer cards remain the soft spot, with revenue flat as partner payments and rewards costs climb. Shares also fell 3.48% in premarket trading after the report, on caution over fourth-quarter markets seasonality and the pace of capital deployment.

Weighing the Discount Against the Returns Gap

Wall Street consensus estimates compiled on InvestingPro put 2027 earnings at $12.78 a share, which pushes the forward multiple below 10 times. InvestingPro data also show a PEG ratio of 0.26 for Citigroup, against 0.75 for Bank of America. Tangible book value per share rose 6% to $101.59, which puts the stock at about 1.2 times tangible book. Management has repurchased $13.3 billion of stock so far this year, more than all of 2025, and has raised its dividend for four straight years. The median analyst price target is $150.71, though earnings revisions over the past 90 days lean negative.

BAC Sees Untapped Merrill Banking Potential: Can Cross-Selling Pay Off?

Bank of America BAC has considerable scope to expand banking relationships within its Merrill Wealth Management franchise. With 67% of Merrill clients maintaining banking relationships, the remaining customer base presents an opportunity to increase lending and deposit penetration. Leveraging its integrated banking and wealth management platform could help the company generate incremental revenues and strengthen client relationships.

BAC offers Merrill clients a broad range of banking solutions, including mortgages, securities-based lending, customized credit facilities and deposit products. By addressing clients' investment and financing needs through a unified platform, the company can capture a greater share of their financial activities. Its established advisor network also provides an advantage in identifying cross-selling opportunities without significant customer acquisition costs.

The company's third-quarter 2026 results reflect growing demand for its wealth management offerings. Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) client balances increased 9% year over year to $5.1 trillion, while average loans and leases rose 13% to $279 billion. During the quarter, Merrill and Private Bank collectively added approximately 5,000 net new relationships with at least $500,000 in assets, highlighting continued client acquisition momentum.

Higher banking penetration could support GWIM's earnings growth by boosting net interest income and diversifying its revenue streams. In the third quarter, segment revenues increased 13% year over year to $7.1 billion, while net income reached $1.5 billion. The pre-tax margin improved to 29% from 27% a year earlier. Further expansion of banking relationships could enhance revenue productivity and operating efficiency.

However, intense competition, deposit pricing pressures and interest rate fluctuations may constrain growth. Clients' preference for maintaining relationships with multiple financial institutions could also limit cross-selling success. Nonetheless, Merrill's sizable client base and BofA's extensive banking infrastructure position the company to capitalize on untapped opportunities, supporting long-term revenue diversification and profitability.

How Are BAC's Peers Capitalizing on Similar Opportunities?

Morgan Stanley MS is expanding banking relationships through its integrated wealth management platform, which combines investment advisory, lending and deposit solutions. In the third quarter of 2026, Morgan Stanley's wealth management revenues increased 10% year over year to $9.1 billion, while loans rose 15.6% to $201.1 billion. Continued growth in lending activities and deeper client engagement could support recurring revenues and strengthen Morgan Stanley's wealth management franchise.

JPMorgan Chase JPM is leveraging its diversified banking platform to strengthen relationships with affluent clients through investment, credit and deposit offerings. In the third quarter of 2026, assets under management increased 13% year over year to $5.2 trillion, while average loans and deposits grew 20% and 5%, respectively. JPMorgan's extensive banking network and comprehensive financial solutions provide opportunities to increase wallet share and sustain growth in wealth management revenues.

title: JPM Flags Higher Rate Risks: Can Its Balance Sheet Stay Resilient?

JPM Flags Higher Rate Risks: Can Its Balance Sheet Stay Resilient?

Trading disclosure

JPMorgan JPM remains focused on maintaining balance sheet resilience amid expectations of structurally higher interest rates. At the Nov. 5 BancAnalysts Association of Boston Conference, Charles Bristow, head of Treasury and chief investment officer, emphasized disciplined duration management, stable operating deposits and rigorous stress testing to navigate interest rate volatility.

Bristow noted that JPMorgan has historically avoided excessive exposure to longer-duration securities, helping limit valuation risks as interest rates increased. Its emphasis on operating deposits linked to payments, custody and checking activities also supports funding stability, although unusually sharp rate increases could pressure deposit costs.

The company's underlying performance reinforces this resilience. During the first nine months of 2026, reported net interest income (NII) increased 11% year over year to $77.9 billion. NII excluding Markets rose 4% to $71.7 billion, supported by deposit and loan growth. JPMorgan expects fourth-quarter 2026 NII of approximately $28 billion, implying full-year NII of $106.2 billion, while NII excluding Markets is projected to be $97.2 billion. Its preliminary 2027 outlook projects NII excluding Markets of nearly $107 billion, reflecting almost 10% growth backed by balance sheet expansion and higher rates.

However, Bristow cautioned that proposed regulatory capital requirements could undermine returns from certain low-risk intermediation activities. Rapid interest rate repricing and tighter systemwide liquidity also pose risks.

Overall, JPMorgan's diversified franchise, disciplined asset-liability management and stable deposit base support its earnings outlook. Nevertheless, regulatory uncertainty, funding costs and interest rate volatility warrant monitoring, suggesting a balanced investment approach.

How are JPM's Peers Expected to Fare in a Higher-Rate Regime?

Two close peers of JPMorgan are Bank of America BAC and Citigroup C.

Bank of America is well-positioned to benefit from higher interest rates, supported by its asset-sensitive balance sheet, fixed-rate asset repricing and loan growth. Bank of America expects 2026 NII to increase approximately 8% year over year. However, higher deposit costs could partly offset these benefits.

Citigroup is positioned to benefit from higher interest rates, given its asset-sensitive balance sheet, loan growth and investment portfolio repricing. Citigroup expects 2026 NII, excluding Markets, to increase in the mid-to-high 6% range year over year. However, rising deposit costs could partly offset these benefits.
